title: Statistics - Lesson 2: Representative Data Practice
description: Practice identifying populations, samples, bias, and careful conclusions.

questions.question: A report claims, "Most Grade 10 learners prefer digital notes." Which group is the population?
options: All Grade 10 learners named in the claim
Only the learners who answered the survey
Only learners who prefer digital notes
questions.explanation: The population is the whole group the claim describes: all Grade 10 learners.

questions.question: A teacher asks the first 15 students who enter the room about the whole class. What type of sample is this closest to?
options: Random sample from the full class list
questions.explanation: The first students to enter are easy to reach, so this is a convenience sample.

questions.question: A large sample can still be biased if it is chosen from only one narrow group.
questions.explanation: Sample size helps, but a biased selection method can still fail to represent the population.

questions.question: In a sample of 40 learners, 28 prefer printed reviewers. What percent prefer printed reviewers? Enter the percent with the percent sign.
questions.explanation: 28 divided by 40 is 0.70, so 70% of the sample prefer printed reviewers.

questions.question: Which sampling plan is usually strongest for a claim about all Grade 10 learners?
options: Randomly select learners from every Grade 10 section
Use only volunteers from a social media post
Ask the first ten students seen after class
questions.explanation: Randomly selecting from every section gives different parts of the Grade 10 population a fair chance to appear.

questions.question: A survey question says, "Do you agree that our excellent library should stay open longer?" What is the main problem?
options: The population is too large to name
questions.explanation: The word "excellent" pushes respondents toward a positive answer, so the wording is not neutral.

questions.question: A poll asks only basketball players about all students' favorite sport. Explain one reason the data may not be representative.
questions.correctAnswer: Basketball players may prefer basketball more than the general student population, so the sample may overrepresent one viewpoint.
questions.explanation: A good answer should connect the sample group to a likely bias in the conclusion about all students.

questions.question: Write one careful sentence using this result: In a random sample of 80 Grade 10 learners, 52 said they prefer group study.
questions.correctAnswer: In this random Grade 10 sample, 52 out of 80 learners preferred group study, giving reasonable evidence that group study is popular among Grade 10 learners.
questions.explanation: The answer should mention the sample result and connect it carefully to the Grade 10 population.
